paper.title_en: Spherical-DAHA predictions for boundary monopole bubbling of non-minuscule 't Hooft lines in $\mathcal N=4$ SYM
paper.abstract_en: We study non-minuscule boundary 't Hooft lines in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ $U(N)$ super Yang-Mills theory with the regular Nahm-pole boundary condition. For one-row charges we construct the spherical-DAHA operator $\mathbf{e}_+h_r(Y)\mathbf{e}_+$ and determine its finite shift expansion and discrete Macdonald spectrum. For the first non-minuscule $U(2)$ coefficient, a local two-minuscule convolution model with Higgs branch $T^*\mathbb{P}^1$ has two Jeffrey-Kirwan residues, while subtracting the determinant intersection-cohomology summand supplies the additional $-\mathfrak{t}$ term. The same transverse $A_1$ calculation, dressed by the spectator-root factor, reproduces the first lower $U(3)$ coefficient. The two residues are the cross terms of the square of the first Macdonald-Ruijsenaars operator and the subtraction realizes $h_2=e_1^2-e_2$, so that this calculation is a geometric realization of the algebraic coefficient, while its boundary-localization interpretation remains conjectural. We then let the operators act on the evaluation functionals at the points $q^λ\mathfrak{t}^ρ$ with $ρ=(N-1,\ldots,0)$, which for minuscule $λ$ coincide, up to a common factor and the order of the entries, with the fugacities of the Higgsing computation of Hatsuda and Okazaki. The zero-shift coefficient at $\mathfrak{t}^ρ$ of the product of the two oppositely oriented operators equals the normalized Neumann Wilson two-point function for every one-row charge, and for $U(2)$ and $r=2$ this equality requires the $-\mathfrak{t}$ term.
